response.text:
I can do this, but I won’t take any destructive action until you explicitly confirm. Please confirm the exact plan below or edit it first.

Planned action (what I would do once you confirm)
- Action: Delete messages (move to Trash) that match all of:
  - Label = "Newsletters"
  - Message date older than 1 year from today (i.e., before 2025-09-05)
- Scope: every message with that label and older than 2025-09-05. (I will delete messages, not whole calendar events.)
- How deletion works / visibility: messages will be moved to your Gmail Trash. They will not be emailed to anyone; only your account is affected.
- Reversibility: messages in Trash can be restored for up to ~30 days; after that they are permanently removed by Google and typically not recoverable.
- What could go wrong: I might delete newsletters you still want (including ones with useful attachments or receipts), or messages you’ve starred/flagged; if a conversation contains both old newsletter messages and newer important messages, removing the old messages could be confusing.

Options to change before I act
- Instead of deleting, I can archive them (keeps them searchable but removes them from the label view? — note: archiving won’t remove the custom label; tell me if you prefer removing the label instead).
- Exclude starred messages, messages from specific senders, or messages with attachments.
- Preview: I can show you the oldest 10–20 newsletter threads/messages for quick approval before bulk deletion.

Please confirm exactly:
1) Proceed to delete all messages with label "Newsletters" dated before 2025-09-05? (yes / no)
2) If yes, do you want to exclude starred messages or any senders, or would you like a preview first? (specify)
3) Delete (move to Trash) vs Archive vs Remove label (choose one)

Once you reply with explicit confirmation and any exclusions, I will proceed.
